subject: Roberts Elementary Safety and State Accountability Ratings
overview: The committee addressed reports of violent student incidents at Roberts Elementary, leading to calls for improved parent notification and program reviews. The body also celebrated the district's move to a Level 2 state accountability rating and approved educational goals for the 2016-2017 school year.

items.title: Routine Approvals
items.summary: Approved the minutes from September 12, 2016, along with bills, payrolls, and the Committee of the Whole report.

items.title: Roberts Elementary Safety Concerns
items.summary: A parent reported multiple traumatic incidents in a third-grade classroom and requested smaller class sizes and better communication from the administration. The committee approved motions for the principal to address the body, the administration to meet with parents, and the superintendent to review student allocations and provide ongoing reports.

items.title: Commendations and Commemorations
items.summary: Recognized the success of the Mystic River Celebration and the Crystal Campbell Peace Garden dedication, and commended Patricia Velie for her service as she leaves the district.

items.title: Complete Streets Traffic Safety
items.summary: Announced a $400,000 grant for street safety improvements, including beacons and curb bump outs at the Brooks School, and approved a motion requesting a state crossing guard for the Fellsway.

items.title: Gifts and Donations
items.summary: Approved the donation of a garden shed from Urban Sheds and accepted 60 backpacks with supplies from Agero for economically disadvantaged students.

items.title: SBIRT Substance Abuse Screening
items.summary: Received a report on the mandatory Screening Brief Intervention and Referral to Treatment (SBIRT) tool for substance abuse prevention in grades seven and nine. Placed on file after discussion of confidentiality and parent opt-out procedures.

items.title: District Priority Educational Goals
items.summary: Approved the 2016-2017 educational goals focusing on new science frameworks, social-emotional learning, and transition to MCAS 2.0.

items.title: School Brains Implementation
items.summary: Received an update on the transition to School Brains software and scheduled further training for teachers and administrators on the grade book system.

items.title: Minuteman Project Update
items.summary: Discussed the regional vocational school district's changes and Medford's plan to contest a proposed capital fee as an unfunded mandate. Placed on file.

items.title: Financial Reports
items.summary: Reviewed the FY2016 year-end closeout and FY2017 current status, noting increased costs in homeless student transportation. Placed on file.

items.title: MBTA Student S-Passes
items.summary: Requested a report on the feasibility and administration of providing discounted MBTA S-Passes to middle school students.

items.title: State Testing and Accountability Results
items.summary: Announced that the district moved from Level 3 to Level 2 in state accountability ratings, though the High School dropped to Level 2 due to test participation rates. Referred to the Curriculum Subcommittee for deeper analysis and requested a report on funding for MCAS prep programs.

items.title: MASC Delegates and Condolences
items.summary: Selected Robert Skerry as delegate and Paulette Van der Kloot as alternate for the MASC conference and extended condolences to the family of Frank Andre.
